name: Endpoint custody, post-hire re-verification, behavior, and payment correlation

attribution.legal_posture: Behavioral or remote-work observations are nonspecific and require corroboration; DTEX defensive practitioner guidance and first-party platform/threat-research guidance supply context, while identity attribution and measured control effectiveness require separate evidence.

caveats: Automated provisioning can accelerate harm when identity assurance, endpoint custody, and least-privilege scoping fail before activation.
Generic guidance for identity assurance and role scoping; automated provisioning can accelerate harm when checks fail before activation.
Hardware-key possession identifies an authentication factor; interview identity, later endpoint operation, and remote delegation remain separate questions.
Low engagement, missed meetings, or remote work are nonspecific review context; attribution requires corroborated signals.
Most incident denominators in the article come from DOJ or secondary reporting and should remain sourced to the underlying primary records.

This records hardware-token control context; DPRK incident or measured anti-DPRK outcome remains unestablished. Hardware-token possession alone leaves interview completion and later endpoint operation unresolved.

statements: Deel recommends role- and time-bound access, SSO/MFA for all worker types, HRIS-triggered provisioning, immediate offboarding revocation, MDM/endpoint controls, and auditable access across employees, contractors, and EOR workers.
limitations: Generic guidance, not DPRK-specific evidence. Automated provisioning can accelerate harm if identity assurance and role scoping fail before activation.

statements: Okta describes new hires completing identity proofing on first login with a pre-enrolled YubiKey, HR and IT teams monitoring transactions, and a read-only API check of legal/preferred first names to reduce legitimate name-mismatch failures.
limitations: This is not a DPRK incident or measured anti-DPRK outcome. Hardware-token possession does not independently establish who completed interviews or who operates a remote endpoint later.

statements: DTEX recommends mapping contractors, vendors, endpoints, and device chain-of-custody rather than relying on a background check as the terminal trust decision.

It recommends live interviews plus post-hire re-verification, contextual review of low engagement or unexplained disappearance, monitoring for suspicious remote access, and correlation of device and payment activity.
The recommendations emphasize that a quiet, timely, technically competent worker can still present insider risk; behavioral indicators require corroboration and should not be used alone.
